prompt: 1000 identical balls are dropped into a pipe of uniform width as shown. How many balls in total are expected to exit at A?

solutions.title: Halve at each split
solutions.body:
At each junction the balls split equally between the two pipes. To reach A a ball must go left at the top junction, left again at the next junction, and left again at the junction above A and B: three halvings. So $A$ receives $1000\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=125$ balls.

**Answer: 125**

prompt: The diagram shows four straight-line segments, two of which are parallel. Determine the size of the angle $y$ in degrees.

solutions.title: Straight angle, then alternate angles
solutions.body:
The angles $3x$, $5x$ and $2x$ lie on a straight line, so $10x=180$ and $x=18^\circ$. The slanted segment crosses the two parallel lines, so $y$ and $3x$ are alternate angles: $y=3x=54^\circ$.

**Answer: 54**

prompt: Ayo and Buhle share a packet of sweets in the ratio 3:5. If Buhle gets 12 more sweets than Ayo, how many sweets did the packet contain?

solutions.title: Ratio parts
solutions.body:
The difference of $5-3=2$ parts is 12 sweets, so one part is 6 sweets. The packet has $8$ parts: $8\times6=48$ sweets.

**Answer: 48**

prompt: If $x\Delta y$ means $y^2+xy$, then determine the value of $t$ if $t\Delta3=21$.
Points $A(7;3)$, $B(4;0)$ and $C(1;3)$ lie in the Cartesian plane. Find the angle $\hat{ABC}$ in degrees.

solutions.title: Slopes
solutions.body:
$BA$ goes 3 right and 3 up (slope 1) and $BC$ goes 3 left and 3 up (slope $-1$). The slopes multiply to $-1$, so the lines are perpendicular: $90^\circ$.

**Answer: 90**

solutions.title: Lengths
solutions.body:
$AB^2=18$, $BC^2=18$ and $AC^2=36$, so $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$ and the angle at $B$ is a right angle.

**Answer: 90**

prompt: There are 65 boys in Grade 9 who play sport. Of these, 35 play soccer and 42 play rugby. How many Grade 9 boys play both soccer and rugby?

solutions.title: Overcount
solutions.body:
$35+42=77$ exceeds 65 by 12, and the boys who play both were counted twice. So 12 play both.

**Answer: 12**

prompt: For a particular assessment, a student has to obtain at least 40% to pass. If the student got 15 marks, but failed by 3 marks, how many marks was the assessment out of?

solutions.title: Pass mark
solutions.body:
The pass mark is $15+3=18$, which is 40% of the total. $18\div0.4=45$.

**Answer: 45**

prompt: If $\dfrac a4=\dfrac9a=\dfrac b{12}$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers, then what is the value of $b$?

solutions.title: Solve for a
solutions.body:
$\frac a4=\frac9a$ gives $a^2=36$, $a=6$. Then $\frac b{12}=\frac64=\frac32$, so $b=18$.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: 60% of the 30 pupils in a class are girls. If $\frac23$ of the class speak Sesotho, what is the smallest possible number of girls who speak Sesotho?

solutions.title: Maximise the boys
solutions.body:
There are 18 girls and 12 boys, and 20 pupils speak Sesotho. The fewest girls speak it when as many boys as possible do: all 12 boys, leaving $20-12=8$ girls.

**Answer: 8**

prompt: Cloud Cycles makes 2-wheeled bicycles and 3-wheeled tricycles. Last week they made 14 cycles in total. If they used 38 wheels, how many tricycles did they make?

solutions.title: Extra wheels
solutions.body:
If all 14 cycles had 2 wheels there would be 28 wheels. The 10 extra wheels each belong to a tricycle (one extra wheel per tricycle), so there are 10 tricycles.

**Answer: 10**

prompt: Three rectangles are placed as shown. If the outer perimeter of the L-shape is 106 units, then what is the area of rectangle A?

solutions.title: Perimeter of an L
solutions.body:
The perimeter of the L-shape equals the perimeter of its bounding rectangle: width $11+17=28$ and height $x+15$ where $x$ is the height of A. $2(28+x+15)=106$ gives $x=10$. Rectangle A is $11\times10$, so its area is 110.

**Answer: 110**

prompt: 12 has six factors, namely 1; 2; 3; 4; 6 and 12. What is the largest 2-digit number with exactly 3 factors?

solutions.title: Squares of primes
solutions.body:
A number has exactly 3 factors only if it is the square of a prime $p$ (factors $1,p,p^2$). The 2-digit squares of primes are $25$ and $49$. The largest is 49.

**Answer: 49**

prompt: The natural numbers are arranged in a regular pattern as shown, with four numbers in each row. If the pattern is continued, what is the 100th number in Column D?

solutions.title: Find the pattern in column C
solutions.body:
Column C holds $3,7,11,15,\dots$, i.e. $4n-1$ in row $n$, so row 100 has 399 in column C. In even-numbered rows the numbers run right to left, so column D holds one less than column C (e.g. row 2: C is 7 and D is 6). So row 100 has $399-1=398$ in column D.

**Answer: 398**

prompt: The speeds of three athletes are in the ratio 3:4:5. The corresponding times taken by these three athletes to complete a race are in the ratio $20:x:y$. Determine the value of $x+y$.

solutions.title: Distance is fixed
solutions.body:
Distance $=$ speed $\times$ time is the same for all three: $3\cdot20=60$. Then $4x=60$ gives $x=15$ and $5y=60$ gives $y=12$. $x+y=27$.

**Answer: 27**

prompt: Four grandchildren live with their grandmother and grandfather. The average age of all six people is 30. The average age of the four grandchildren is 12. If the grandfather is 6 years older than the grandmother, how old is the grandfather?

solutions.title: Sums of ages
solutions.body:
All six sum to 180; the grandchildren sum to 48; so the grandparents sum to 132. With $g$ the grandfather: $g+(g-6)=132$, so $g=69$.

**Answer: 69**

prompt: The diagram shows a large rectangle that has been subdivided into two smaller rectangles (on either side) and a square (in the middle). Determine the perimeter of the large rectangle. (The dimension 8 is marked along the top, across the left rectangle and the square; the dimension 10 is marked along the bottom, across the square and the right rectangle.)

solutions.title: Add lengths
solutions.body:
Let the square have side $x$. The top dimension 8 covers the left rectangle and the square; the bottom dimension 10 covers the square and the right rectangle. So the large rectangle has width $8+10-x$ and height $x$. Perimeter $=2(18-x)+2x=36$.

**Answer: 36**

prompt: A dartboard consists of two circles. The shaded region is $\frac25$ of the total area. Two darts are thrown randomly at the dartboard. If both darts hit the board, what is the probability, as a percentage, that one dart hits the shaded region and the other hits the non-shaded region?

solutions.title: Two orders
solutions.body:
The probability of shaded then non-shaded is $\frac25\cdot\frac35=\frac6{25}$, and the same for the other order. Total $\frac{12}{25}=48\%$.

**Answer: 48**

prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length 2 cm. What is the maximum number of points that can be placed inside and on the edges of the triangle such that no two points are closer than $0{,}5$ cm ($0.5$ cm) to one another?

solutions.title: Triangular lattice
solutions.body:
Divide each side into 4 parts of $0.5$ cm and join to make a triangular lattice of small equilateral triangles of side $0.5$ cm. The lattice has $1+2+3+4+5=15$ points, each pair at least $0.5$ cm apart, so 15 points are possible.

**Answer: 15**

prompt: A train travels at a constant speed. It takes 21 seconds for the train to completely cross a 445 m long bridge, and 16 seconds to completely cross a 320 m long bridge. How long is the train in metres?

solutions.title: Equal speeds
solutions.body:
Let the train be $L$ metres long. Crossing a bridge means travelling bridge length plus $L$. $\frac{L+445}{21}=\frac{L+320}{16}$ gives $16L+7120=21L+6720$, so $5L=400$ and $L=80$.

**Answer: 80**

solutions.title: Extra time
solutions.body:
The extra $445-320=125$ m takes the extra $21-16=5$ s, so the speed is $25$ m/s. In 16 s the train travels $400$ m, which is $320+L$, so $L=80$.

**Answer: 80**

prompt: A room contains 99 boys and 1 girl. How many boys need to leave so that the boys make up 96% of the people in the room?

solutions.title: Girl is 4%
solutions.body:
The single girl will make up 4% of the people, so there must be 25 people in total: 24 boys and 1 girl. So $99-24=75$ boys leave.

**Answer: 75**

prompt: Cylinder A has a radius of 8 cm and a height of 20 cm. Cylinder B has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 30 cm. The two cylinders are filled with water to the same height ($h$). When the water from cylinder B is poured into cylinder A then cylinder A is filled to capacity. What was the initial height ($h$) of the water in the cylinders?

solutions.title: Volumes
solutions.body:
Water in A: $\pi\cdot8^2h=64\pi h$. Water in B: $\pi\cdot4^2h=16\pi h$. Capacity of A: $64\pi\cdot20=1280\pi$. So $80\pi h=1280\pi$ and $h=16$.

**Answer: 16**

prompt: Two identical rectangles, each measuring 4 cm by 8 cm, overlap as shown. Determine the shaded area in $\text{cm}^2$.

solutions.title: Rhombus
solutions.body:
The shaded shape is a rhombus. Let its side be $x$ (the slanted side along the diagonal-corners) and consider the right triangle with legs 4 and $8-x$ and hypotenuse $x$: $x^2=16+(8-x)^2$, so $16x=80$ and $x=5$. The rhombus has base 5 and height 4: area $20\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: 20**

prompt: There is a sequence of seven positive integers. From the third number onwards, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly before it. If the seventh number is 2025, what is the smallest possible value of the first number in the sequence?

solutions.title: Express in the first two terms
solutions.body:
With first terms $x,y$ the sequence is $x,y,x+y,x+2y,2x+3y,3x+5y,5x+8y$. So $5x+8y=2025$, and $8y=2025-5x$. We need $2025-5x$ divisible by 8; since $2025\equiv1$ and $5x\equiv1\pmod8$ means $x\equiv5$, the smallest is $x=5$ (then $y=250$).

**Answer: 5**

prompt: Four envelopes are labelled $A,B,C,D$. Four matching cards are labelled $a,b,c,d$. In how many ways can the cards be placed in the envelopes so that each envelope contains exactly one card and NO envelope contains its matching card?

solutions.title: Derangements
solutions.body:
Envelope $A$ can get $b$, $c$ or $d$. Say it gets $b$; then the arrangements of the rest with no matches are $B a,C d,D c$; $B c,C d,D a$; $B d,C a,D c$: 3 each time. Total $3\times3=9$.

**Answer: 9**

prompt: Two cyclists are riding in opposite directions on a circular track. One rides at a constant speed of 2 m/s while the other rides at a constant speed of $x$ m/s. The two cyclists pass one another every 30 seconds. If the length of the circular track is greater than 200 metres, what is the smallest integer value of $x$?

solutions.title: Relative speed
solutions.body:
Riding in opposite directions, they close at $x+2$ m/s and meet every time they cover one lap together: track length $=30(x+2)=30x+60$. We need $30x+60>200$, i.e. $x>4.67$, so the smallest integer is $5$.

**Answer: 5**
